subject: refactor(io)!: add context to IO.Open and IO.Remove (#2067)
body:
* refactor(io)!: add context to IO.Open and IO.Remove

`io.IO.Open` and `Remove` now take `context.Context`, matching `BulkRemovableIO.DeleteFiles`.
`blobfs.FileIO.Remove` forwards the caller context so deletes honor cancellation/deadlines.
`maintenance.WithCleanupDeleteFunc` now takes `func(context.Context, string) error`.

Breaking change: all `IO` implementations/callers must pass a context, and custom delete callbacks must update their signature.

Part of the v1.0 API cleanup in #2062.

Signed-off-by: laskoviymishka <laskoviymishka@gmail.com>

* fix(io): keep failure cleanup immune to caller cancellation

Moving blobfs Remove onto the caller context made cleanup after a failed
operation fail with it: when the failure was itself a cancellation or a
timeout, the removal was canceled too and files that used to be cleaned
up were left behind on object stores. Before this change Remove ran on
the context captured when the FileIO was built, so a canceled caller
never reached it.

Run those cleanup paths on context.WithoutCancel(ctx), which keeps the
context's values (tracing and similar) but not its cancellation:

- doCommit's deferred removal of orphaned manifest lists
- the hadoop catalog's temp metadata file and version claim removals
- sql removeUncommittedMetadata, which already loaded the filesystem
  without cancellation but removed with the caller context
- the removal of a partially written delete manifest in
  writeDeletedEntries
- the Glue S3 Tables commit rollback

Paths where removal is the requested work (orphan cleanup, PurgeFiles,
expire snapshots' post-commit deletes, drop namespace and drop view)
keep the caller context so they stay cancellable.

Tests use an IO that rejects Remove on a canceled context, as blobfs
does, to check that doCommit and removeUncommittedMetadata still clean
up after a cancellation.

Also reword the IO.Open doc to say implementations may use ctx to bound
the open, since no backend does yet, and drop the comments claiming
every backend ignores ctx, which would go stale once one honors it.

Signed-off-by: laskoviymishka <laskoviymishka@gmail.com>

* refactor(table): thread ctx through the manifest content cache IO

The manifest content cache that landed on main wraps the scan FileIO
with the old context-free Open and Remove, so the merge no longer
built. Give manifestContentCacheIO the context-taking signatures.

Opens of other paths and Remove forward the caller's context. The
cached manifest path keeps using the scan context captured in wrap,
because the manifest readers that call Open have no caller context to
pass and would otherwise drop the scan's cancellation. The cache's
own opens, including the population read and the fallback opens, use
that same context.

Signed-off-by: laskoviymishka <laskoviymishka@gmail.com>

subject: fix(table): validate DV replacement on add (#2054)
body:
Two paths still let a row delta commit more than one live deletion vector
for a single data file:

- Same-delta duplicate DVs on the fast-append path. findReplacedLiveDVs
  collapses added DV references into a set, and when the data file has no
  live DV yet the scan returns nothing; with no RemoveDeletes,
  validateRemovedDeletes (which held the only duplicate-added-DV check)
  never runs, so AddDeletes(dvA, dvB) for one data file committed two live
  DVs. Hoist the duplicate-added-DV check into validateAddedDeletionVectors,
  run unconditionally on every commit path.

- Concurrent first-DV additions across a commit retry. Two writers based on
  a snapshot with no DV for a data file both pass findReplacedLiveDVs. After
  one commits, the other's add-only delta is replayable: doCommit rebuilds
  the manifest list against the refreshed parent but did not re-check DV
  uniqueness, so the retry could inherit the concurrent DV and commit a
  second one. Add validateNoConcurrentReplacedDVs to RowDelta.validate: on
  retry it walks the concurrently committed delete entries and rejects a
  live DV added for a data file this delta also adds a DV for. It is a no-op
  on attempt 0 (no concurrent snapshots), and a removal-carrying delta is
  non-replayable, so there are no removals to reconcile on retry.

Tests: TestRowDeltaFastAppendRejectsDuplicateAddedDVs covers the fast-append
duplicate, and TestRowDeltaRejectsConcurrentFirstDVOnRetry drives the
two-writer retry through the OCC scenario catalog and asserts the retry is
rejected before a second commit attempt.

subject: refactor(table): add Table.ManifestProvider and move inspect onto public (#2151)
body:
* refactor(table): add Table.ManifestProvider and repoint inspect onto public APIs

Introduce a public ManifestProvider (via Table.ManifestProvider) that reads a
snapshot's manifest list through the table's shared, bounded manifest-list cache
and resolves the table FileIO once per provider. It exposes Manifests,
DataManifests, and FS, keeping the internal snapshotManifestSet cache and
sharedSnapshotManifestFSF unchanged behind it.

Manifests and DataManifests return iter.Seq[iceberg.ManifestFile] over the
cache-owned slice. That keeps the no-copy cache hit from #2112 while giving
callers outside the package no way to mutate the shared cache, which a
borrowed []ManifestFile in a public signature could not guarantee.

Repoint the metadata-inspection code off the table package internals it reached
into (the unexported manifestSet / manifestSetWithFSF methods, the fsF field, and
the metadata / metadataLocation fields) and onto public accessors
(Table.ManifestProvider, Table.FS, Table.Metadata, Table.MetadataLocation). The
provider is created once per inspection so the all_* metadata tables still
resolve the backend once and share the manifest cache. AllManifests now fills
its record batches from a reused chunk buffer instead of slicing the manifest
list, with the same batch boundaries; no behavior change.

This leaves the inspection surface depending only on public table APIs, in
preparation for moving it to a dedicated table/inspect package.

* refactor(table): drop ManifestProvider.DataManifests and pin cache sharing

DataManifests had no caller and no test, and it would become permanent
public surface on release. Drop it until a caller needs it; the
data-only view stays available inside the package.

Add a test that reads the same snapshot through two providers from one
Table and checks the manifest list is opened once, so building the
provider without the table's shared cache now fails.

Document that a provider keeps the result of its first FileIO
resolution, error included, so it is meant for one operation and a new
provider is needed to retry.

Read and write the same bytes as Java's StandardEncryptionManager and
iceberg-rust, so files can be exchanged between implementations.

  generated locally and stored raw; there is no KMS call per file. The
  reader derives the plaintext length from file_length.

  iceberg-rust use, and accept it on read.

  WithStandardDataKeyLength.

- Document that ErrOutputFileClosed is only returned after a successful
  Close.

Tests decode the writer's output with a stdlib-only AGS1 decoder, read a
stream built the same way, and check a hand-encoded key metadata vector.

subject: fix(table): pin guarded refs in RollbackToSnapshot and ExpireSnapshots (#2301)
body:
* fix(table): pin guarded refs in RollbackToSnapshot and ExpireSnapshots

Since #2248 the SQL, Glue, Hive and Hadoop catalogs report a failed
commit requirement as ErrCommitFailed, so with commit.retry.num-retries
above zero doCommit retries it and rewrites the commit branch's
AssertRefSnapshotID to the refreshed head. RollbackToSnapshot and
ExpireSnapshots rely on that assertion to detect a concurrent change, so
a stale rollback could discard a peer's append and a stale expiry could
remove snapshots the moved branch still retains. REST was already
affected through 409 responses.

Pin the refs these operations guard, including branches the transaction
staged, using the same mechanism as Transaction.AssertRefSnapshotID.
Pins and the staged updates are now published under one lock, so a
failed apply leaves no pin. A pinned assertion that no longer holds
after refresh fails the commit without spending the rest of the retry
budget.

Signed-off-by: Harrison Crosse <harrison@crosse.dev>

* fix(table): skip guards for a no-op ExpireSnapshots

An ExpireSnapshots call that finds nothing to expire stages no update,
but it still pinned every ref. In a transaction that also appends, the
pin on the commit branch stopped the append from rebasing onto a peer's
commit, so the retry failed instead of succeeding.

Return without adding requirements or pins when there is nothing to
expire, while still rejecting a transaction that has already been
committed.

Signed-off-by: Harrison Crosse <harrison@crosse.dev>

subject: feat(table,rest): enforce the catalog's scan-planning-mode directive (#2162)
body:
* fix(table): add ScanPlanningDirective() accessor on table

Previously, the table returned by a LoadTable() on a REST catalog did
not have any way of exposing what scan planning mode the catalog is
trying to enforce on this table. In cases where the catalog is enforcing
server-side scan planning, the caller would have to rely on errors
and/or missing files through the Scan() interface, to realize that
server-side scan planning is necessary.

This change exposes a ScanPlanningDirective() function on a table.Table
that exposes this value as returned from LoadTableResponse. If the catalog
is not imposing any particular scan planning mode,
ScanPlanningDirectiveUnknown is returned.

* fix(table): carry scan-planning directive state explicitly

Address review feedback on the ScanPlanningDirective accessor:

- WithScanPlanningDirective now takes (value, ok) so absence is explicit
  and a comma-ok map read can be passed straight through.
- Add WithScanPlanningDirectiveFrom to copy a table's directive verbatim;
  RefreshTableCredentials uses it instead of reconstructing the raw value
  from SavedConfig, which could report the wrong directive for externally
  built tables.
- Drop the positional loadConfig parameter from tableFromResponse; load
  paths pass the directive as a caller option instead.
- Rename ScanPlanningDirectiveUnknown to ScanPlanningDirectiveNone and
  document that it only means "no directive" with a nil error.
- Use a switch over the valid directives.
- Add coverage for Commit, StagedTable, Refresh, CreateTable,
  RegisterTable, and LoadTable followed by a credential refresh.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(catalog): report stale commit requirements as ErrCommitFailed and add commit conformance tests (#2248)
body:
* test(catalog): add table commit tests to the catalog conformance suite

Cover the CommitTable path, which every catalog implements but the suite
did not exercise: create-time properties, property set/remove, schema
evolution, a commit whose requirement went stale under a concurrent
writer, and a commit through a handle to a dropped table.

* fix(catalog): classify failed commit requirements as ErrCommitFailed

SQL, Hive, Glue and Hadoop validated commit requirements locally and
returned the bare requirement error, while REST maps the same case
(409) to table.ErrCommitFailed. A stale writer on those catalogs was
therefore never retried by the commit retry loop, and a commit to a
dropped table did not report ErrNoSuchTable.

Validate requirements through one shared helper that reports a failure
on a missing table as catalog.ErrNoSuchTable and any other failure as
table.ErrCommitFailed. Retries remain opt-in through
commit.retry.num-retries, which defaults to 0.

subject: fix(catalog/rest)!: make OAuth token refresh context-aware and singleflight (#2265)
body:
AuthHeaderWithContext checked ctx once and then called Token()
synchronously, so a caller blocked on a stalled token endpoint until the
refresh client's Timeout regardless of its own deadline. Concurrent
callers each ran their own refresh in turn behind the token source's
mutex.

Share one in-flight Token call per manager with a singleflight.Group and
let the caller wait for it only until ctx is done. The refresh keeps
running, bounded by the refresh client's Timeout, and its result serves
later callers. AuthHeader goes through the same group.

BREAKING CHANGE: Oauth2AuthManager is no longer comparable. The type has
only unexported fields and pointer-receiver methods, so no caller can
hold two meaningful values to compare.

Signed-off-by: Ilia Demianenko <ilia.demianenko@clickhouse.com>

subject: feat(catalog): add table lifecycle conformance tests and fix rename-to-existing errors (#2165)
body:
* feat(catalog): add table lifecycle tests to the catalog conformance suite

Add ListTables, DropTable, DropMissingTable, RenameTable,
RenameTableToExisting and RenameMissingTable to catalogtest, gated by a
new Config.SupportsRenameTable flag. SQL, REST and Hive opt in; Hadoop
does not implement rename.

Related to #1691

* fix(catalog): return ErrTableAlreadyExists when renaming onto an existing table

The new RenameTableToExisting conformance test found that REST and Hive
returned untyped errors for this case. REST now maps 409 to
ErrTableAlreadyExists, matching CreateTable. Hive checks the destination
while holding the rename locks, matching its create path.

Related to #1691

* fix(hive): detect non-Iceberg tables at rename destination

CheckTableExists only recognises Iceberg tables, so a non-Iceberg Hive
table at the destination was invisible to the pre-check and AlterTable
would return a raw metastore error.  Switch to a raw GetTable call so
any table (Iceberg or not) at the destination is rejected with
ErrTableAlreadyExists.

Also strengthen the rename conformance test to assert that the table
UUID survives the rename, catching backends that silently recreate
instead of renaming.

* test(catalog): verify unsupported rename and rename metadata preservation

Address review feedback on the table lifecycle conformance tests:

- When SupportsRenameTable is false, run RenameTableNotSupported instead
  of skipping the rename suite, asserting RenameTable returns
  iceberg.ErrNotImplemented and leaves the source table in place. The
  Hadoop catalog now wraps that sentinel. Reference #1097 in the field
  doc.
- Assert that rename preserves the table metadata location alongside
  its UUID, catching backends that rename by recreating the table.

subject: test(catalog/rest): run conformance suite against external REST catalogs, with Polaris in CI (#2190)
body:
* test(catalog/rest): run conformance suite against Apache Polaris

Add an opt-in integration test that runs the catalog conformance suite
against an Apache Polaris server, a second REST implementation alongside
the Java REST fixture. Testing against two servers surfaces client-side
divergences that a single fixture can mask, such as the rename error
mappings fixed in #2165 and #2173.

The test is skipped unless POLARIS_URI is set, so the integration job is
unaffected. POLARIS_CREDENTIAL and POLARIS_WAREHOUSE are required once
it is enabled. CONTRIBUTING.md documents starting a local Polaris server
with file storage, including the CATALOG_MANAGE_CONTENT grant the client
needs because it requests vended credentials by default.

Signed-off-by: Richie Bachala <richie.bachala@gmail.com>

* test(catalog/rest): move Polaris setup into a script

Address review feedback on the Polaris conformance test:

- Move the bootstrap out of CONTRIBUTING.md into
  internal/recipe/setup-polaris.sh, next to the compose file so CI can
  reuse it. CONTRIBUTING keeps a short pointer.
- The script bounds the readiness wait and prints the container logs if
  Polaris never comes up, fails on a missing token (jq -e) and surfaces
  error bodies (curl --fail-with-body), and replaces its container on
  each run so it can be rerun.
- Explain the readiness override: Polaris refuses to start with FILE
  storage otherwise, since it flags FILE as a severe security risk.
- Require POLARIS_CREDENTIAL to be a client_id:client_secret pair.
- Log which outcome RenameTableToSelf took, so a backend's self-rename
  behavior is visible in a passing run.

Signed-off-by: Richie Bachala <richie.bachala@gmail.com>

* test(catalog/rest): show Polaris error bodies and log real self-rename error

- setup-polaris.sh: route API calls through a helper that prints the
  server's error body on failure. --fail-with-body alone did not surface
  it, because each body went into jq or /dev/null. Use 2-space indents
  to match the repository's other shell scripts.
- RenameTableToSelf: log the error a rejected self-rename returned,
  rather than a fixed message that would misreport an unexpected error.

Signed-off-by: Richie Bachala <richie.bachala@gmail.com>

* test(catalog/rest): generalize Polaris conformance into an external REST catalog test

Per review on #2190, replace TestPolarisCatalogConformance with
TestExternalRestCatalogConformance, which runs the conformance suite against
any REST catalog configured through REST_CATALOG_URI, _CREDENTIAL, _SCOPE and
_WAREHOUSE. Only the URI is required.

Add make integration-setup-polaris and integration-external-rest, which
default to the local Polaris server, and run them in the Go Integration
workflow on the Spark 3.5 leg, since Polaris does not depend on Spark.

subject: ci: add apidiff check for incompatible API changes (#2166)
body:
Part of the v1.0 freeze work in #2062. After the 1.0.0 tag, any breaking
change to the exported API needs a /v2 module, so we want CI to catch them.

The new "API compatibility" workflow runs golang.org/x/exp/cmd/apidiff in
module mode on every pull request. It exports the API of the base branch
tip the PR merges onto and compares the merged result against it. Internal
packages are skipped. The list of incompatible changes goes to the job
summary.

Until 1.0 we still make intentional breaks, so a break only fails the check
when the PR title does not declare it with the Conventional Commits "!"
marker (for example "refactor(io)!: ..."), which the repo already uses for
breaking changes. Editing the title re-runs the check. After the tag, the
title escape hatch can be dropped so any break fails.

If apidiff itself fails, for example because the base or the PR does not
build, the script prints the error and exits 2, so a broken build is not
reported as an API break.

The logic lives in dev/check-api-compat.sh so it can also be run locally
against any base ref. CONTRIBUTING.md now mentions the check and the "!"
convention.

subject: refactor!: remove ManifestFile.FetchEntries and DataFile.DistinctValueCounts (#2179)
body:
refactor!: remove deprecated ManifestFile.FetchEntries and DataFile.DistinctValueCounts

ManifestFile.FetchEntries loaded every entry into memory and took no
context. Use ManifestFile.Entries, which streams entries as an iterator:

    for entry, err := range mf.Entries(fs, discardDeleted) {
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }
        // use entry
    }

or ReadManifest when a slice is needed.

DataFile.DistinctValueCounts and DataFileBuilder.DistinctValueCounts exposed
distinct_counts (field 111), which the spec deprecates in every format
version. Writers already omitted the field, so the setter had no effect on
the wire. The Avro field stays on the data file struct, so legacy manifests
that carry it still decode, and writers continue to omit it. The tests now
check both on the struct, and a codec test checks that the entry schema has
no field 111.

This is a breaking change for callers of the removed methods.

Part of the v1.0 API cleanup in #2062.

subject: fix(io): treat ADLS Gen2 / OneLake directory blobs as directories in blobfs WalkDir (#2180)
body:
* fix(io): walk hierarchical namespace directories in blobfs WalkDir

On ADLS Gen2 accounts with a hierarchical namespace (such as OneLake),
every directory is also stored as a 0-byte blob named after it, with no
trailing slash. gocloud's fs.FS treats any key with an exact object as a
file, so WalkDir stopped at the walk root and reported it as the only
file. Orphan cleanup then listed the table location as its only orphan.

WalkDir now walks a small adapter over the bucket. A key with objects
under it is a directory, and a 0-byte blob named after a child directory
is hidden from listings. Trailing-slash markers on flat stores behave as
before, and the walk makes one listing per directory instead of an
existence check plus a listing.

Fixes #2159

subject: refactor(table): export SnapshotLogEntryAsOf for metadata-table time travel (#2150)
body:
* refactor(table): export SnapshotLogEntryAsOf for metadata-table time travel

Promote the snapshot-log time-travel resolver from the unexported
snapshotLogEntryAsOf to the exported SnapshotLogEntryAsOf, so code outside the
table package (the forthcoming table/inspect package) can resolve a snapshot as
of a timestamp without reaching into table internals.

Pure rename plus repoint of the in-package callers (the as-of-timestamp scan,
Table.SnapshotAsOf, and the metadata_log_entries inspection). No behavior change.

* docs(table): state the SnapshotLogEntryAsOf tie-break and test it

On equal timestamps SnapshotLogEntryAsOf keeps the earliest entry in log
order. That matches Java's SnapshotUtil.nullableSnapshotIdAsOfTime, which
now picks the greatest eligible timestamp with a strict comparison, so a tie
also resolves to the first entry there, and Java's metadata_log_entries
table resolves through the same function. Behavior is unchanged; the doc
comment now says so instead of implying order never matters.

Add a table test for the exported function covering an empty log, no
eligible entry, an out-of-order log, inclusive and exclusive matching, and
equal timestamps.

subject: test(catalog): table-lifecycle conformance slice with cross-namespace rename and error-mapping fixes (#2173)
body:
* feat(catalog): add table lifecycle tests to the catalog conformance suite

Add ListTables, DropTable, DropMissingTable, RenameTable,
RenameTableToExisting and RenameMissingTable to catalogtest, gated by a
new Config.SupportsRenameTable flag. SQL, REST and Hive opt in; Hadoop
does not implement rename.

Related to #1691

* fix(catalog): return ErrTableAlreadyExists when renaming onto an existing table

The new RenameTableToExisting conformance test found that REST and Hive
returned untyped errors for this case. REST now maps 409 to
ErrTableAlreadyExists, matching CreateTable. Hive checks the destination
while holding the rename locks, matching its create path.

Related to #1691

* fix(hive): detect non-Iceberg tables at rename destination

CheckTableExists only recognises Iceberg tables, so a non-Iceberg Hive
table at the destination was invisible to the pre-check and AlterTable
would return a raw metastore error.  Switch to a raw GetTable call so
any table (Iceberg or not) at the destination is rejected with
ErrTableAlreadyExists.

Also strengthen the rename conformance test to assert that the table
UUID survives the rename, catching backends that silently recreate
instead of renaming.

* test(catalog): verify unsupported rename and rename metadata preservation

Address review feedback on the table lifecycle conformance tests:

- When SupportsRenameTable is false, run RenameTableNotSupported instead
  of skipping the rename suite, asserting RenameTable returns
  iceberg.ErrNotImplemented and leaves the source table in place. The
  Hadoop catalog now wraps that sentinel. Reference #1097 in the field
  doc.
- Assert that rename preserves the table metadata location alongside
  its UUID, catching backends that rename by recreating the table.

Signed-off-by: Richie Bachala <richie.bachala@gmail.com>

* test(catalog): add cross-namespace rename conformance tests

Extend the table lifecycle conformance suite with two rename cases where
catalog behavior tends to diverge:

- RenameTableAcrossNamespaces: a table moves to another namespace, keeps
  its UUID, and is listed only in the destination.
- RenameTableToMissingNamespace: renaming into a namespace that does not
  exist returns ErrNoSuchNamespace and leaves the source table in place.

The second case exposed a REST divergence. The spec's rename 404 covers
both a missing source table and a missing destination namespace, and
the client mapped every 404 to ErrNoSuchTable. Discriminate on the
error type, following loadFunction, so a missing namespace reports
ErrNoSuchNamespace as Hive and SQL already do.

Signed-off-by: Richie Bachala <richie.bachala@gmail.com>

* fix(catalog): address rename review feedback

- rest: route the rename 404 NoSuchNamespaceException split through
  withErrorTypeOverride, so the refinement is status-gated. A 5xx or
  401/403 carrying that type no longer reads as ErrNoSuchNamespace.
  Add tests for those statuses and for an empty or unknown error.type
  falling back to ErrNoSuchTable.
- hive: map an AlterTable already-exists rejection to
  ErrTableAlreadyExists, covering a destination created after the
  pre-check by a writer that skips the HMS locks.
- catalogtest: on a rejected rename-to-existing, assert both
  identifiers still name their original tables, not just that they
  exist.
- hadoop: assert the ErrNotImplemented sentinel instead of matching
  the error message, in both the unit and integration tests.

Signed-off-by: Richie Bachala <richie.bachala@gmail.com>

* address round-2 review: self-rename, 409 type override, mock annotation

- Add RenameTableToSelf conformance test: asserts ErrTableAlreadyExists
  and verifies the table is unchanged, pinning the from==to divergence
  the reviewer flagged.
- Fix the status-gating comment and add a test for 409 carrying
  NoSuchNamespaceException, documenting that the type override applies
  to any mapped status (not only 404).
- Annotate the concurrent-create mock with a note that the
  InvalidOperationException text is verbatim HMS output.

* test(catalog): accept both self-rename outcomes in conformance suite

RenameTableToSelf asserted ErrTableAlreadyExists, which fails against
the Java REST fixture: its JdbcCatalog returns early when from == to,
treating a self-rename as a no-op success. Java's catalogs disagree on
this (JdbcCatalog and InMemoryCatalog no-op, HiveCatalog rejects), and
neither the REST spec nor Java's CatalogTests define the outcome.

Assert only what every catalog agrees on: the rename succeeds or returns
ErrTableAlreadyExists, and any other error fails. Either way the table
must keep its UUID and metadata location and be listed exactly once.

Signed-off-by: Richie Bachala <richie.bachala@gmail.com>

* docs(catalog): cite apache/iceberg#4448 for self-rename semantics

Record why RenameTableToSelf accepts both outcomes: when REST rename was
added, a request-level check rejecting source == destination was dropped
so servers could decide, and Java's catalogs now differ.

Signed-off-by: Richie Bachala <richie.bachala@gmail.com>

subject: fix(view): stop MetadataBuilder.Build from growing the version log (#2109)
body:
* fix(view): stop MetadataBuilder.Build from growing the version log

view.MetadataBuilder.Build appended the pending history entry to
b.versionLog, so building the same builder again added the entry again:
three builds gave three version-log entries. Append to a copy instead.

On the table side, updateSnapshotLog wrote the pruned log back into
b.snapshotLog. Running it again gives the same result, so this did not
change any output, but it was still a side effect of Build. It now
returns the pruned log (as updatedSnapshotLog) and leaves the builder
unchanged, like the metadata log since #2095.

lastUpdatedMS stays cached on the builder after the first Build, so
repeated builds report the same timestamp; that is now documented.

Closes #2108

Signed-off-by: Animesh Kumar <kanimesh187@gmail.com>

* fix: make repeated builds stable and pin the pruning and expiry paths

- table: compute lastUpdatedMS per Build instead of storing it on the
  builder, so a build after more changes gets a fresh timestamp.
- view: keep the UUID generated for a new view on the builder and reuse
  it, so repeated builds describe the same view; SetUUID still works.
- Document on both Build methods that they can be called more than once.
- Tests: build twice after RemoveSnapshots, the view expiry path with
  VersionHistorySizeKey=1, a builder from existing metadata, a stable
  generated UUID, and a fresh timestamp after more changes.

* test(view): use the embedded Metadata methods directly

* fix: keep Build's guarantee scoped to the logs

Per review, Build only guarantees that it doesn't write the version log
or the snapshot log back to the builder.

- table: keep lastUpdatedMS cached on the builder, as Java's
  TableMetadata.Builder does, and say when it is set.
- view: keep generating the UUID per build when none is assigned, as
  Java's ViewMetadata.Builder does.
- Tests: drop the timestamp and UUID assertions, build a three-entry
  base version log with a history size of 2, and pin the [A, A] snapshot
  log after moving main back to A between builds.
- Say which calls move lastUpdatedMS after the first Build.
- Document that updatedSnapshotLog never aliases b.snapshotLog and
  derives pruning from b.updates.

* fix: adapt to bun v1.3.0 and lz4 v4.1.33 in the gomod_updates bump

bun v1.3.0 deprecates DB.AddQueryHook in favour of WithQueryHook, which
returns a copy of the DB with the hook attached instead of mutating it.

stay installed; golangci-lint's SA1019 failed every unit job.

lz4 v4.1.31+ makes Writer.Close fail when the written length differs
from SizeOption, so the puffin tests could no longer build frames that
advertise a wrong content size. Write a valid frame and rewrite its
content-size field and header checksum instead. The reader-side lz4
now also verifies the content size, so the size-mismatch case is
rejected by lz4 before puffin's decoded-size check; assert
lz4.ErrInvalidContentSize there.
